source_name: World Bank corporate procurement - 'Electronic payments in North Macedonia' RFx
why_relevant: A live procurement notice revealing that the World Bank with the National Bank is assessing the electronic-payments-acceptance landscape in MK - names the workstream, scope and timing, and signals a forthcoming public diagnostic plus consultant ecosystem around MK acquiring/POS.

source_name: World Bank Global Findex database (North Macedonia microdata/indicators)
why_relevant: The only demand-side, internationally comparable series on MK account ownership, digital payment usage and card/mobile behaviour; anchors addressable-market sizing for payment vendors.

source_name: European Payments Council - SEPA scheme participant register and MK press releases
why_relevant: The EPC register lists, bank by bank, which MK PSPs adhere to SCT/SCT Inst/SDD and from which date - a hard, structured indicator of which MK banks have completed SEPA-readiness projects (and therefore bought/upgraded payment hubs). EPC press releases date the geographical-scope decision and operational readiness (ORD 5 Oct 2025).

source_name: ECB Data Portal - payments statistics datasets (PAY/PSS) and semi-annual releases
why_relevant: Provides the methodological and comparative frame for card/terminal/transaction statistics across Europe and comparator non-euro-area countries; MK itself is outside the reporting perimeter, but the series is the benchmark against which NBRM payment statistics are read. Semi-annual press releases give EU aggregates and country notes.

source_name: Internet Archive Wayback Machine + CDX API (MK bank and vendor domains)
why_relevant: The only route to deleted vendor customer/reference lists, old MK bank e-banking and card pages, discontinued product names and pre-merger bank sites (e.g. Komercijalna banka, Stopanska banka, NLB, Halkbank, Sparkasse, and vendor sites such as asseco/ASEE, Pexim, Printec, Nextsense, Duna, Seavus). CDX API enables systematic enumeration of snapshots by domain and URL prefix.

source_name: Asseco SEE (ASEE) news/press archive - regional vendor announcements incl. MK
why_relevant: Primary competitor-vendor press stream for the SEE region; observed item announces delivery of 10 new Diebold Nixdorf ATMs to Komercijalna Banka. ASEE's MK entity descends from Pexim Skopje, so the archive documents the incumbent vendor footprint and its OEM partnerships (Diebold Nixdorf, IBM, Fujitsu).

source_name: EMIS (ISI Emerging Markets) - company profiles for MK banking-IT firms
why_relevant: Commercial emerging-markets aggregator carrying structured MK company profiles (legal entity, executives, partner list); the Asseco SEE DOOEL profile lists technology partnerships (IBM, EMC2, Fujitsu-Siemens, Wincor-Nixdorf). Useful for building the vendor actor map with registry-grade identifiers.

source_name: bne IntelliNews - Southeast/emerging Europe country coverage (North Macedonia)
why_relevant: Analyst-style regional outlet covering MK macro, FDI and banking; observed MK-specific reporting on greenfield FDI performance. Complements SeeNews with longer-form context and occasional bank/fintech deal analysis.

source_name: European Western Balkans - EC report analysis portal
why_relevant: Specialist regional outlet that summarises and cross-compares EC enlargement-report findings per country and year; a fast pointer into which chapters moved, and a durable secondary record when EC page structures change.

source_name: EBRD newsroom and project portal - North Macedonia financial institutions
why_relevant: EBRD names counterpart MK banks and the purpose of each facility - e.g. Go Digital Western Balkans credit lines to Sparkasse Bank Skopje and NLB Banka Skopje, and loans to ProCredit Bank. Signals which banks are funding digitalisation projects and when, i.e. leading indicators of vendor demand.

source_name: EIB press and Western Balkans digital-development publications
why_relevant: EIB Global funds digital and financial-infrastructure programmes in the Western Balkans; press releases and studies identify programme scope and partner banks, complementing EBRD for the financing side of MK bank IT modernisation.

source_name: The Paypers - payments industry aggregator (MK/SEPA coverage)
why_relevant: Payments-trade aggregator that picks up MK scheme and processor news for an international audience (e.g. North Macedonia and Moldova joining SEPA); useful early-warning feed for MK payment-vendor announcements that never appear in local media in English.

source_name: AppsRunTheWorld - Asseco CBS customer database
why_relevant: Commercial analyst database that compiles core-banking-system customer lists from public and proprietary sources; a rare structured route to which banks (potentially incl. MK) run Asseco CBS, complementing archived vendor reference pages.

source_name: Interoperable Europe Portal / OSOR - North Macedonia country report
why_relevant: EC-hosted annual country report on MK digital-government, interoperability and e-ID/e-services infrastructure - the public-sector rails (identity, e-payment of public fees) that bank and payment vendors integrate with.

source_name: BIS central bankers' speeches - National Bank of North Macedonia governor speeches
why_relevant: BIS republishes NBRM governor speeches in English, which regularly set out payment-system modernisation plans (instant payments, SEPA, fintech regulation) earlier and more explicitly than formal reports; an English-language archive of MK central-bank intent.

source_name: NBRSM — Регистар на платежни институции (Register of Payment Institutions)
why_relevant: Statutory public register under the Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems; enumerates every licensed non-bank payment institution, simplified-access payment institutions, their agents and branches. This is the definitive competitor/partner list for the MK payments market and the anchor for vendor-to-PI mapping.

source_name: NBRSM — Регистар на оператори на платните системи (Register of Payment System Operators)
why_relevant: Lists licensed payment-system operators (KIBS AD Skopje, MIPS operated by NBRSM, card scheme/processing operators where licensed). Directly names the infrastructure incumbents Printec-type vendors must integrate with or compete around.

source_name: NBRSM — Македонска платежна инфраструктура / Macedonian Payment Infrastructure
why_relevant: Describes the national payment infrastructure stack (MIPS RTGS, KIBS retail clearing, card systems) and links to each operator. Establishes the actor map for any market-entry or integration thesis; the EN mirror gives canonical English names.

source_name: NBRSM — КИБС page (Clearing House KIBS AD Skopje, retail netting system)
why_relevant: Regulator's description of KIBS, the multilateral netting operator for small-value payments (<1,000,000 MKD). Pointer into KIBS AD itself, a key infrastructure counterparty/competitor and a channel for vendor case studies.

source_name: NBRSM — NBStat statistical database / API
why_relevant: NBRSM's structured statistics platform with documented API access (search result quotes NBRSM terms permitting API use). Machine-readable path to payments and banking time series without scraping HTML pages.

source_name: Закон за платежни услуги и платни системи (Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems), consolidated text on NBRSM
why_relevant: PSD2/EMD2-transposing law (Official Gazette 90/2022, in force 1 Jan 2023) that creates the licence categories, the registers themselves, and open-banking/API obligations. Defines the taxonomy every other source in this cell uses; the consolidated PDF (144-25) shows amendment cadence.

source_name: NBRSM — Регулатива за платните системи и платежните услуги (payments rulebook hub)
why_relevant: Index of all secondary legislation (одлуки, упатства) for payment systems and services — licensing, security of payment services, strong customer authentication, fees, reporting. Regulatory change here is the earliest signal of upcoming vendor/integration demand.

source_name: NBRSM — Одлука за издавање дозволи и согласности на платежна институција и институција за електронски пари и за содржината и начинот на водење на регистрите
why_relevant: The decision (Official Gazette 289/22 per search snippet) that specifies exactly which fields the registers must contain and how they are maintained — the schema definition for parsing the register pages, plus the licensing bar new entrants must clear.

source_name: NBRSM — Годишна информација за движењата во плаќањата (annual payments developments report)
why_relevant: NBRSM's recurring annual analysis of payment developments (instrument mix, card/POS/e-banking penetration, system throughput). The closest thing to a national payments oversight report and the best narrative source for market-trend framing.

source_name: NBRSM — Национален совет за платните системи (National Payment Systems Council)
why_relevant: Multi-stakeholder body (NBRSM, banks, KIBS, ministries, card schemes) whose composition and minutes reveal who sits at the table on national payments strategy — a partnership/stakeholder map and an early view of instant-payments and standards initiatives.

source_name: NBRSM — Банки / Штедилници (banks and savings houses directory) and Банкарска супервизија и регулатива
why_relevant: Authoritative list of licensed banks and savings houses — the buyer universe for payments technology in MK, and the counterpart set to the non-bank PI/EMI registers. Supervision section adds prudential rulebooks and supervisory reports.

source_name: NBRSM — Листа на водечки броеви на банките (bank leading/BIC-style code list)
why_relevant: Canonical bank identifier list used in MIPS/KIBS routing. Low glamour but high value as the join key for reconciling entity names across registers, statistics and market data.
